title: Shed and Shuttle
mech: A monolithic printed comb of twelve springy warp fingers sits under the deck; sliding a sculpted cam bar into the channel beneath it pushes a chosen set of warp posts up through the surface, where they physically block their lanes, and the lanes left flat are the only legal moves for everyone.
blurb: Four weavers share one printed loom deck: each turn you swap the cam bar that decides which of the twelve lanes stand open, then throw your shuttle down one of them before the next player changes it again.
idea: The board computes its own legal moves. A single printed warp comb holds twelve compliant cantilever fingers, each with a cam follower underneath and a 6mm post on top that rises through a slot in the deck. Eight interchangeable cam bars each carry a distinct thirteen-cell profile of raised and flat cells; pushing one into the channel under the comb lifts exactly the posts its raised cells sit beneath, and a raised post stands across its lane so a shuttle physically cannot pass. That twelve-bit vector is the entire game state and it is held mechanically, not on paper. On your turn you must first pull the loaded bar and seat a different one at notch 1 or notch 2 - the second notch shifts the same bar one lane along and yields a completely different shed, so eight bars are really sixteen patterns - and only then may you slide your shuttle down an open lane and drop a thread tile into its lowest empty slot. Because you re-cut the shed before you weave, and the player after you weaves into the shed you just left, the real decision is never where to place a tile but which lift pattern you are willing to hand to the opponent on your right. Lanes score by tile majority with lowest-slot tie-break, so a bar that opens your five-point lane and closes the three cheap lanes an opponent could answer in is worth more than the tile itself. No dice, no cards, no hidden information: pattern selection, area majority, and a printed compliant mechanism that makes illegal moves mechanically impossible rather than merely against the rules.
identity: like Azul + a printed jacquard heddle comb whose cam bars raise real warp posts across the lanes, so the piece you load decides which moves exist for every player
